#1464. Pat Cummins' remarkable 68-minute press conference took a clear-eyed and devastating aim at Usman Khawaja's integrity - Australia are in a civil war with no obvious resolution, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

Published: 05:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 05:21 EST, 13 November 2026

Pat Cummins is either the greatest actor in world sport – or the claim that the whole Australian team knew about the sandpaper plot in South Africa eight years ago is a figment of Usman Khawaja’s imagination.

After Cummins’s remarkable press conference in Sydney on Friday morning, in which he called Khawaja’s various assertions ‘complete and utter nonsense’ and questioned the validity of their friendship, it was hard to discern any common ground, much less spot a middle way.

According to the blue corner, everyone was in on the scam, sandpaper was used not just at Cape Town but in the previous Test at Port Elizabeth, and there was a team meeting to discuss the question of collective responsibility.

According to the red, those who knew about the plan did not include the bowlers, nothing untoward happened at Port Elizabeth, and there was no meeting.

The only thing that can be said for certain after another tumultuous 24 hours for Australian cricket was that the two corners are now polar opposites, each eyeing the other with suspicion and incredulity. Barring an improbable climbdown, the twain can never meet.

Cummins, it must be said, eased into his work after an emotional start behind a lectern at the Cricket Central venue in Sydney’s Olympic Park. He began by stating his basic position, then invited questions, which for the next hour and a bit he handled with aplomb and a degree of statesmanship.

Pat Cummins held a remarkable press conference in Sydney to address the sandpaper claims

Speaking for more than an hour, Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s various assertions as ‘complete and utter nonsense’ and questioned the validity of their friendship

This will not please those who still find it impossible to believe that Cummins and his fellow seamers on that trip, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, knew nothing of the scheme that led to bans for three batsmen – Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.

After all, as any bowler will tell you, the idea that the condition of their most prized possession might be altered without their noticing is as absurd as trying to persuade a batsman to walk out without his favourite willow.

And yet. Cummins stuck to his guns, in contrast to Khawaja’s appearance on the ABC on Wednesday evening, when he repeatedly declined to name Cummins as one of the guilty party. And while Khawaja reacted to his TV grilling by cancelling media engagements, Cummins made it clear he would be answering every question that came his way.

Whichever side you believe, and whatever the doubts that remain, his press conference grabbed the momentum from Team Khawaja.

It also made the previous day’s appearance by Mitchell Marsh, Australia’s white-ball captain for the next three weeks against England, all the more bizarre. By refusing to engage with any of the questions raised by Khawaja’s autobiography, Marsh – himself a veteran of South Africa 2018 – did little to dispel the suspicion that Khawaja had a point.

And that in turn encouraged the view that Cummins, who called his own press conference without the knowledge of Cricket Australia, might be about to come clean.

Instead, he doubled down on the denial he and his bowling colleagues had issued in 2021, but now went further, taking a clear-eyed and devastating aim at Khawaja’s integrity.

‘Usman is a friend, but friends aren’t casual with each other’s lives and reputations,’ said Cummins. ‘He’s dealt with the way he’s presented his story in a very casual manner and it affects a lot of people. That’s what I’m grappling with at the moment, because I don’t think that’s OK. It’s not what friends do.’

Cummins plainly intended this to be his final word on the matter, but the problem facing Australian cricket is that the sore may never properly heal.

David Warner then hit back at Cummins and accused him of 'throwing Khawaja under the bus'

Only a couple of hours after Cummins finished, Warner – at Perth’s Optus Stadium as a TV pundit for the first ODI between Australia and England – was being asked for his view, and he didn’t hold back, repeating his belief that Khawaja’s version of events was ‘the truth’.

He added: ‘I really, really support him. I actually feel for him at the moment. I feel that the captain today threw Uzzy under the bus and I’m very, very disappointed about that.’

Disappointment. It’s mutual, and it’s everywhere. Cummins provided a brief distraction, but it doesn’t change the fact that this is a civil war with no obvious resolution.

Offered the chance to kick Australian cricket while it was down, England made humiliating contact with fresh air on the opening day of their eight-match white-ball trip.

Only hours after Pat Cummins had added a twist to the sandpaper saga by dismissing Usman Khawaja’s claims that the whole squad knew about the ball-tampering plans in South Africa eight years ago as ‘complete and utter nonsense’, Harry Brook’s side were blown away for 131 in the first ODI – having at one stage been 65 for eight.

Australia then romped home by seven wickets with more than 26 overs in hand to take a 1–0 lead into the second game of this three-match series in Adelaide on Sunday. For England, anyway, complete and utter nonsense felt about right.

It is not quite a year since they began their Ashes campaign here at the Optus Stadium by being bowled out in 32.5 overs in their first innings and 34.4 in their second – before stumbling to a 4–1 defeat.

Now, they obligingly split the difference, dismissed in 33.4 as Mahli Beardman, a 21-year-old fast bowler from Dunsborough, a couple of hours drive down the coast from Perth, picked up six for 34 – the best figures for Australia by an ODI debutant.

His first victim was Joe Root, caught behind for a painful 17 off 36 balls, and his second Brook, who had made only a single when he fidgeted fatally outside off stump.

That might have been enough to satisfy most newcomers, but Beardman had barely started. Jordan Cox made two before edging a poke, and Sam Curran top-edged a pull to fine leg for a duck.

When Liam Dawson, yet to score, squeezed a drive to backward point, Beardman had five wickets in 28 balls – not bad for a player whose only previous taste of international cricket had come in a T20 in Pakistan in January.

He then ended a lively last-wicket stand of 29 by removing Jofra Archer, who had just driven him down the ground for four. It was the only authentic boundary England managed off his bowling: the other, a streaky inside edge from Root, summed up the problems posed by his pace, bounce and accuracy. As bids for a place on next summer’s Ashes tour go, this was hard to ignore.

‘Laying in bed last night, that’s not what I had planned,’ said Beardman, who was taken under his wing by Australian fast-bowling legend Dennis Lillee after a mutual friend spotted him as a young teenager bowling at a bin down the side of a house. ‘It was an incredible game and it all happened so fast.’

If England had learned lessons from their collapses in the last year’s Test here, they showed little sign of being able to implement them. Players drove on the up, as they had so heedlessly a year earlier, and failed to cope with the Perth bounce.

England head coach Brendon McCullum was critical of his side's failure to adapt to the pitch, and called on them to learn from their mistakes going forward.

'It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline,' said McCullum. 'There are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away. We probably knew we were in for a low-scoring contest, but we expected to get a few more runs than 130.

'We're disappointed but there are some good lessons for us. If you look towards the World Cup in South Africa there’s going to be some pitches there that will test us from a bounce point of view.'

And all this after they had played a warm-up game at the WACA – a grievous omission before the Ashes – and trained with such intensity that white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen had declared it the best practice session he had seen from an England team.

In the event, their top-scorer was Gus Atkinson, who hit an unbeaten 29 from No 10, including England’s only six.

Mitchell Marsh, stroke-less in the previous day’s press conference, put that into perspective by clearing the ropes four times during a 29-ball half-century, while Cooper Connolly – dropped by Tom Banton at midwicket on five – hit two sixes himself.

England’s only consolation had come at the start of Australia’s reply, when Atkinson bowled Travis Head first ball off the inside edge. Head it was who had taken care of Australia’s fourth-innings chase here a year ago, thrashing a 69-ball century that knocked the stuffing out of Ben Stokes’s attack.

Instead, it was Marsh who went for his shots, stopped only when he flicked Jamie Overton to Ben Duckett at deep midwicket, by which time Australia were already halfway there. For a few hours, at least, no one was talking about sandpaper.

#1463. Thuram and Locatelli absences leave Juventus midfield thin for four games in 12 days

Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

The table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”

Leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

If they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Anton Stach, who was accidentally blocked by team-mate Jayden Bogle, and Gudmundsson both went close in the first half.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1461. France star Desire Doue is left with gruesome tooth injury after PSG youngster suffered elbow smash to the face during Les Bleus' dismal defeat by Italy

Published: 06:41 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 13 November 2026

France star Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after being hit with a nasty elbow in France's 3-1 defeat to Italy in the Nations League.

The PSG winger was left in need of some emergency dental work by Italy's Davide Frattesi who caught the 21-year-old in the mouth while shielding the ball.

In his post match interview French boss Zinedine Zidane, when asked if Doue had lost a tooth, replied: 'Yeah I think so. We’re going to take him straight there, a tooth has come loose I think, we’ll take care of him starting tomorrow.'

It was a poor day all round for the Frenchman who not only had his tooth dislodged but was also unable to impact a poor game for Les Blues in which the Azzuri beat them at the San Siro.

To compound Doue's misery it was the offender Frattesi who scored Italy's second goal in the 3-1 win just six minutes before he performed some unorthodox dentistry.

The Lazio midfielder's goal completed the Italians' comeback after going 1-0 down to a Michael Olise goal just ten minutes in before Inter Milan's Francesco Esposito levelled things up just 16 minutes later.

Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after receiving an elbow in the mouth from Davide Fratessi

Fratessi got away with just a yellow card as Italy beat the French 3-1 at the San Siro

Frattesi gave Italy the lead early on in the second half before Esposito netted his second from the spot to put the game out of reach.

Speaking after the game Zidane was surprisingly positive about his team's performance despite the loss, saying that losing is, 'part of the process.'

The French then went onto say: 'The most important thing is creating chances. Hitting the post had an impact, but I'm not disappointed.

'I would have been if we hadn't created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren't at the right level off the ball.'

The World Cup winner was not entirely positive however, later saying: 'in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively.'

The victory put Italy level on points with the French in Group A with both sides having won three drawn one and lost one.

But France will have an opportunity to right their wrongs and return to the top of the group on Sunday as they welcome Turkey.

But if Italy beat Belgium on the same day the French will have to settle for second.

#1459. GdS: 3-4-2-1 or 3-4-1-2 – how Amorim’s formation could change with January addition

AC Milan are tempted by the idea of signing Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi, but how would Ruben Amorim’s system change?

There has been plenty of talk about January signings, but as much as they would be good to bring, they have to be the right fit. After all, signing a name without thinking ahead will only be problematic. So, the right calculations must be made by Amorim and the recruitment team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) looked at how Amorim’s system could change with the arrival of Endrick or Tresoldi and it’s a pretty simple idea.

With Endrick, there would be ‘fewer adjustments’ thanks to his versatility and also his ability to play in the formation already. So, it would see him playing behind the striker alongside Christian Pulisic or Alphadjo Cisse.

For Tresoldi’s arrival, things would have to change. He’s played most of his career as a lone striker, but that would probably change. Instead, he’d probably make up a two-man strike force, alongside Ramos, and then Christian Pulisic or Alphadjo Cisse would play behind him.

It’s a logical choice, but it would mean Amorim would have to change his ideas mid-season. Ultimately, the mercato will choose the route of the Portuguese’s team.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

For either of those two formations to work, we first need proper wingbacks. And define the midfield. Because here’s the catch, I don’t really get – does he want to play wingbacks or inverted wingbacks on the flanks?

Because that too defines the midfield. Playing with regular wingbacks doesn’t require so much defensive cover in the middle as the wingbacks add to the density there. Final third is reserved for inverted playmakers and a striker. Playing inverted wingbacks, that’s a different story. Inverted wingbacks are usually more attacking oriented and as such like to push higher up and get involved in the last third. That exposes the midfield. And this is the version Amorim plays as his strategy is to overload opponents half and penalty area from the flanks inside.

So in any case we’re potentially short on either the flanks or in midfield. And here I don’t see Athekane taking the LWB spot as an inverted wingback like suggested in some reports. He’s not an inverted wingback and will just be wasted.

Amorim’s wingbacks aren’t inverted though… that’s why he doesn’t use Alexis as LWB

Amorim wants his wingbacks to be good in 1v1 and be able to beat the defender. He doesn’t use Alexis as a LWB because Alexis isn’t good in 1v1.

For years having no clear identity and building squads to match no system have caused a mess.

#1458. Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

#1457. Mauricio Pochettino is CONFIRMED as new Man United manager: Departing USA boss speaks out as he agrees to succeed Michael Carrick - but faces race against time for first game

Published: 07:02 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:51 EST, 13 November 2026

Manchester United have confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become their new head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will replace Michael Carrick who was sacked following 10 months in charge on Friday, after United agreed to pay more than £10million to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his new job as United boss on Wednesday. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

There were no comments from Pochettino or United officials in Friday’s press release confirming his appointment because he remains contracted to US Soccer.

Pochettino said in the USMNT's statement: 'The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honors of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.'

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday, but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week.

United sources say that Pochettino’s experience, philosophy, personality and skill-set make him well suited for the job, as well as his record of developing individual talent and building excellent team cultures.

Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as the Manchester United manager

Michael Carrick was sacked after the club made their worst start to the season in 40 years

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’

Earlier in the week, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am on Thursday morning and was dismissed.

He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He became the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season.

United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

'His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'

Sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick indicated.

United feel that the squad are far better than their position in the Premier League shows

They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

It has been a campaign in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and they are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league.

Pochettino's United travel to Anfield on November 22 before a Champions League clash at Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino's first home game against Brentford and then away match at Newcastle.

#1454. Zhegrova plays 82 minutes in Kosovo’s 0-0 with Israel before Dublin decider for second

With Edon Zhegrova in the starting line-up, ten-man Kosovo held Israel to a goalless draw, a result that leaves them second in Nations League Group B3. The run-out gives a Juventus forward who rarely starts for his club valuable match fitness while Pierre Kalulu is injured.

In Pristina, the Juventus forward Edon Zhegrova was Kosovo’s main attacker against Israel.

Zhegrova tested Israel’s defence a couple of times in the first half but faded after the break, according to TuttoJuve. Dion Kacuri came on in his place.

Below Kosovo, Ireland have 5 points and Israel 3. Austria beat the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on the same Saturday.

Kosovo’s campaign has been uneven. They opened by beating the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on 24 September. Three days later they lost 3-1 away to Austria on 27 September. On matchday 3, they had also drawn 0-0 with Israel.

The final round pairs the Republic of Ireland with Kosovo and Israel with Austria. That leaves Ireland, sitting just below Kosovo, hosting the side directly above them. Zhegrova is set to be central to Kosovo’s hopes of holding on to second place.

For Juventus, the significance lies in the minutes. Zhegrova has started only once since joining the club. He sits low in Spalletti’s pecking order and has mostly featured in short spells off the bench.

More than 80 minutes as Kosovo’s focal point gives him match fitness. That could prove useful before Juventus face Venezia in Serie A and Omonia in the Europa League.

The squad is stretched. Scans at J|medical on 9 November found a low-grade injury to Pierre Kalulu’s left biceps femoris. The defender had felt muscle discomfort in his left thigh after the draw at Fiorentina. France withdrew him from their squad. The midfield is also short of bodies.

Spalletti has made clear he sees potential in the winger. “Edon se si completa un po’ può diventare un crack,” the coach said. If Edon rounds out his game a little, he can become a star.

First comes Dublin. Kick-off at the Aviva Stadium is at 7.45pm UK time, with second place in the group at stake.

#1453. Michael Carrick speaks out on his Man United sacking for the first time - and admits 'we've not had the results lately' - as Mauricio Pochettino replaces him

Published: 07:48 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 08:08 EST, 13 November 2026

Michael Carrick has released his first public statement on his Manchester United sacking, calling the job an 'immense privilege' in a classy 411-word tribute to the club's supporters.

The statement, released a little over 24 hours after his dismissal was confirmed, read: 'Dear United Fans, I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

'There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

'With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It's different to anywhere else.

'Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

'It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day. I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

Michael Carrick has broken his silence on his sacking by Manchester United

'We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

'I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

'That means more than a win or two. That's what makes you who you are. That's why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

'A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn't have asked for any more. I'm incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.

'To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

'And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we've shared. I wish you all the very best for what's ahead.

'I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it.

'I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on. Michael.'

The statement follows his former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that Carrick had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of the United legend.

Carrick was left in the lurch by the club's hierarchy - but continued to attend training on Tuesday and Wednesday – amid widespread reports that he would imminently be relieved of his duties.

The classy statement follows Carrick former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that he had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of his dismissal

Neville told Sky Sports News: 'In the last 24-48 hours it's been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who's a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino.

'It's just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you'd be getting sued.

'The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it's just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership.

'I don't think anybody comes out of this well at all.'

Less than an hour prior to Carrick's statement United confirmed his replacement, Pochettino, will take the reins after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the US’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his new job as United boss on Wednesday.

His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week due to his remaining contracted to US Soccer.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

#1451. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after big-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1449. Nascar, Nets, Big 12 and MSE: Yormark’s appointment and how he can help Milan

AC Milan were introduced to a new name this week: Brett Yormark. But who is he and what does he bring to the table?

With Milan’s announcement of a new company – Milan Sport and Entertainment – a new CEO was appointed to oversee things and develop the Milanese sporting project for RedBird and that CEO is Yormark.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For those who are unfamiliar with the new hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE company.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

In terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

After his early experience in basketball, he then moved away from the track and back onto the court where he joined the Brooklyn Jets as their new CEO. Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

From there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime shows.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment company, he leaves behind a role with Big 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

Given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the company take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as big as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.

#1448. Harry Kane reads letters from his kids: England captain close to tears as his four children write to him after he broke the Three Lions appearance record

Published: 05:47 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:12 EST, 13 November 2026

Harry Kane had to compose himself and hold back the tears while reading beautiful letters from his children after breaking the England appearance record.

The 33-year-old earned his 126th cap and scored in the 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday night, with the Wembley crowd celebrating his achievement and Ballon d'Or triumph.

And on the following morning, there was a surprise in store for the England skipper, who was visibly taken aback on camera when presented with letters from his four children, nine-year-old Ivy, eight-year-old Vivi, five-year-old Louis and three-year-old Henry, who he shares with wife Kate.

'Wow, that’s uh a bit of a surprise,' Kane said as he examined the letters and artwork. 'I think you guys are trying to make me cry on camera.'

He opened the first one before reading aloud: 'To Daddy, I love you very much and I want you to know that I’m very proud of you and also you are the best footballer in the world, the most kind Daddy in the world and the best striker in the world.

'I would like to celebrate you playing the most games for England by holiday together and eating ice cream.

Harry Kane was on the verge of tears as he read touching letters from his four children

'My favorite thing about you is you never give up and I love all things you do for us. Love Ivy.'

Dewy-eyed Kane then reflected: 'I wasn’t expecting this beautiful letter. Thank you Ivy. I love you. I've got one here from Vivian as well.'

'Dear Daddy, I’m so happy and proud of you. I love you because you are hard working and make the best fried eggs. I want to celebrate with you by going fishing, going down the water slides and having a cinema trip as well. Love from Vivi.'

Kane then said: 'Yeah, you’ve caught me by surprise here to be honest with you. I’m trying to just uh, stay strong for the camera. Thank you Vivi, love you.'

Then came the letters from Kane's two sons, Louis and Henry.

Louis' read: 'To Daddy, I love you so much because you train and work so hard. My favorite thing we do together is play football and cricket together. I love when you play England football because you score goals and we get to sing Vindaloo. I want to celebrate with you by making an ice cream house with sweets inside. Love Louis.'

'Thank you Louie, love you, boy. This last one is from Henry,' Kane said.

The short and sweet note from his youngest went: 'Daddy, you are the winner. Vindaloo! Love Henry.'

Kane walked onto the pitch with his children, (L-R) Henry, Ivy, Vivi, Louis on Thursday night

Kane showed the artwork and hand-written letters to the camera as he read them

Kane then pointed the endearing scribble to the camera, saying: 'He’s drawn me a lovely picture there. Love you, Henry. Thank you, beautiful messages from my wonderful family.'

Kane, who lives with his family in Bavaria and recently signed a new deal worth £400,000-a-week at Bayern Munich, brought the whole clan, including his parents, to Wembley for his big night on Thursday.

He walked out onto the hallowed turf with his four children, admired a gigantic tifo of himself in the crowd, posed for pictures with the gleaming Ballon d'Or trophy and was given a commemorative shirt by Prince William.

Kane is a devoted family man in addition to being the world's best footballer and took a moment to say a few words about his children at the Ballon d'Or ceremony last month.

He said: 'To Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

Prince William presented Kane with a commemorative framed shirt with 126 on the back

'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'

Kane passed Peter Shilton as the record appearance-maker for England on Thursday and took his tally of goals for the national team to 92.

His penalty put England 2-1 up and they would not relinquish their lead. He'll next be in action against Spain on Sunday.

#1447. Fighter who ambushed UFC star in bloody hotel brawl is punished: Abu Dhabi court dishes out six-month prison sentences and fines - including £61k for filming shocking attack

Published: 09:58 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:57 EST, 13 November 2026

Usman Nurmagomedov and his entourage have been swiftly punished with prison sentences and fines in Abu Dhabi after their shocking hotel attack.

Nurmagomedov set upon UFC star Merab Dvalishvili on Wednesday, slapping him in the lobby of Yas Hilton hotel in a revenge mission filmed by his friends.

The Georgian-American Dvalishvili then retaliated and fought back with his cameraman as the melee rapidly descended into complete mayhem. Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised and the attackers were quickly detained by the authorities.

In just two days, their punishments have been decided by the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, who published the findings on social media.

Six of the attackers were given six-month prison sentences and ordered to pay £61,000 each in fines. They will also be immediately deported  when their sentences end.

They were described as having 'caused panic, disturbed public security and  endangered lives'.

Two of Nurmagomedov's associates were fined £10,000 each for 'disturbing public security and assaulting others'.

Usman Nurmagomedov (left) was the one who initiated the brawl by slapping Merab Dvalishvili - his brother Umar (right) lost a title shot against the Georgian last year

The Abu Dhabi court shared this post online confirming the punishments for the attackers

And the other two members of the group who recorded the assault were given six-month sentences, £61,000 fines and confiscation of the devices used.

Dvalishvili had been due to fight in a RAF wrestling event on Saturday. CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein released a statement confirming the fighter is back.

He said: 'I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.

'We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us.'

Nurmagomedov and his team's violent ambush was four months in the making.

Back in July, Dvalishvili was competing in a RAF event in Georgia, which is a freestyle wrestling show the UFC allow their fighters to compete in outside of the day job.

While milling around at the event, a Dagestani wrestler and friend of Umar, Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, confronted Dvalishvili about refusing to entertain a rematch of any kind with Umar.

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday

'I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody (Gadzhimagomedov) came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand,' Dvalishvili told Ariel Helwani.

'And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realize, "Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him?"

'It’s between me and Umar… I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads.'

After Gadzhimagomedov squared up to him, Dvalishvili shoved him in the neck, shouting: 'What's your problem, b***h!'

The situation, unlike the hotel brawl that escalated into a complete bloodbath, was quickly defused and there was a child in close proximity.

Usman wanted to take revenge on behalf of fellow Dagestani Gadzhimagomedov and also his brother Umar, who lost against Dvalishvili in a title shot last year.

In the footage of the hotel attack, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man said a couple of words to him and slapped him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

He tried to fight back but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too. Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview

He said in a video, bloody and bruised as he received treatment: 'What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

'You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.'

His companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'

Dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It shows your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. This is nothing for me, but it shows what kind of people you guys are. P***ys do this bro. We are warriors.'

#1446. Crystal Palace: Four signings that would be perfect for Thomas Frank in January

Thomas Frank is set to replace Pierre Sage as the manager of Crystal Palace and will be aiming to turn their fortunes around.

Palace are bottom of the table and have shown serious signs of decline this season after the loss of Oliver Glasner in the dugout. Sage just wasn’t able to get the same kind of results as his predecessor over his short reign and has paid the price early.

All Palace can hope now is that they’ve appointed Brentford Frank rather than Tottenham Frank. It could be an ideal opportunity for him to get back on track and redeem his reputation.

But he’ll need all the help he can get to turn this around.

Under Sage, Palace have had comfortably the worst defensive record in the Premier League, conceding 24 goals after 10 games.

Losing their two best centre-backs in successive transfer windows in 2026 hasn’t helped. Marc Guehi went to Manchester City in January before Maxence Lacroix joined Chelsea in the summer.

Palace have failed to replace them adequately. They’ve brought in a couple of temporary solutions on loan but need to think about the long term.

They might have to be savvy in January to find a good solution, looking beyond the usual places.

One player they’ve been linked with recently is Lecce defender Gabriel, who would be a good fit for Frank’s tactics if they can win the race.

Good in the air and alert when the ball’s on the ground, the 21-year-old is ready for his next step and a Premier League move could suit.

During his time at Brentford, Frank was able to help plenty of players improve and Gabriel could be the right kind of defender to work with in the short and long term.

Frank was delighted to sign Gallagher for Spurs last January. He won’t have been so delighted to be sacked four weeks later.

But with Gallagher falling behind in importance for Spurs this season, could he become available again?

If so, he could bring fresh energy into the Palace midfield. Adam Wharton hasn’t quite looked the same player there this season and could probably use some help to get back to his usual standards.

Gallagher could easily do the legwork. He also knows what it takes to play for Palace after impressing there on loan from Chelsea during the 2021-22 season, a spell that included eight goals from 39 games.

Palace could also do with improving their attack. Jean-Philippe Mateta is clearly unsettled, Jorgen Strand Larsen hasn’t got going and Eddie Nketiah isn’t up to scratch either.

Could Richarlison be worth a call? He’s been completely frozen out by Spurs, where Frank had a better opinion of him than Roberto De Zerbi does.

It’s anyone’s guess what Richarlison wants as his next step. But going to Palace would allow him to link back up with a familiar manager and stay in London, too.

The Brazilian is versatile enough to play as a lone striker or in support of another if Palace want to persist with Strand Larsen, Mateta or Nketiah as well.

If Frank wants to look further back, to happier times with Brentford, he might have a hard time convincing anyone to reunite with him given the current positions of both clubs.

But considering Hickey isn’t starting regularly for Brentford, with Michael Kayode ahead of him in the hierarchy at right-back, we wonder if he might be tempted.

Frank rated Hickey highly during their time together. It’s easy to forget the versatile full-back is still only 24.

Palace had to replace Daniel Munoz this summer and his successor Anan Khalaili has been hit and miss so far. Hickey would be someone Frank could trust to offer more security at wing-back.

Frank shut the door on a Brentford exit for Hickey before but what if he turned out to be the man to get him out of the Gtech Community Stadium after all?

#1443. Former Old Firm rivals reveal how clubs walked a fine line between rivalry and respect...and even stopped by for tea and sympathy in times of trouble!

Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026

They have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm. Yet in the autumn of 2026 they cavort around Toryglen with an almost juvenile vigour.

They have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm. Yet they are outlining plans and strategy for a vital, growing movement.

The two meetings are separated by two sets of stairs. On the ground level, men of pensionable age and beyond play walking football. Just above sit Campbell Ogilvie, former secretary of Rangers and president of the Scottish FA, and Eric Riley, once company secretary and director of Celtic.

They are both on the board of Walking Football Scotland, an organisation that now has more than 5,000 people playing the game across 160 clubs, with participants ranging from 40 to 93.

The venerable statesmen of the Scottish game may be perceived to be rivals, but only in matters on the pitch. They sit in an office in the south side of Glasgow and reminisce about how they first met 50 years ago when playing five-a-sides and then renewed that rivalry in their professional life.

As the Glasgow rivals now seem regularly at odds, both men recalled a time when friendship was paramount amid the sporting mayhem.

Former Rangers secretary Campbell Ogilvie and ex-Celtic director Eric Riley are firm friends

‘The two clubs always had a good relationship back in those days,’ said Ogilvie, now 76 and still playing football. ‘We wanted to beat each other — naturally. But off the field we had a very close relationship.’

He told a remarkable story that backs that assertion.

‘There was one day I was at Ibrox in the early 1980s when the team was not doing so well. The phone rang and it was Sean Fallon, Jock Stein’s former Celtic assistant. I had known Sean from my days with the Scottish League and he said: “I know you’re going through a rocky spell, so I’m coming over for a cup of tea”.

‘Over he comes. So there was a very close relationship in those days. I’m not there now and for all I know there still is. But certainly, when I was there and Eric was at Celtic, we could talk to each other.’

Riley, 69, agreed: ‘Absolutely. John McClelland (former Rangers chairman) was one we could talk to. And Martin (Bain, former chief executive) I suppose, when he came along a bit later. Between myself and Peter Lawwell (former Celtic chief executive and chairman) the relationship between the clubs off the field was actually quite strong. But on the field we still wanted to win.’

Ogilvie added: ‘There was a respect. And I go back to the Willie Waddells and the Willie Thorntons, there was that respect. More recently that was there with the likes of Jack McGinn and so on.

‘We had a good relationship but it’s fair to say that there was no social media in those days. You know all the toxic stuff that can bring.’

The traits of respect and sporting competitiveness have been obvious in both men since they first met half a century ago. ‘We played five-a-side football at Scotstoun before the football careers started. It was just casual games,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We were in our early 20s. Eric was an accountant and I think those games were arranged through accountants.

‘I played youth football when I was 16 and, 60 years down the line, playing football is still a major part of my life.’

Ogilvie began walking football eight years ago and Riley soon after. ‘I suffer from Parkinson’s, amongst other things,’ said Riley. ‘I was getting assistance through Stobhill Hospital and the physiotherapist there, who specialises in Parkinson’s patients, got in touch to say there was a project going on at Toryglen where they were playing walking football and assessing you to see what the benefits may or may not be.’

Ogilvie and Riley are both on the board of Walking Football and have played a big role in its rise

Riley agreed to take part. ‘I really enjoyed it because you are back playing football again, you have the camaraderie and you have the home baking which I never really get at home.’

Riley had a hip replacement in March and admitted: ‘I have not played since then. I miss it. I play a few other things which are more and more difficult. I play tennis.’

His tennis history is illustrious as he played with Judy Murray in Scottish championships. ‘She went off to the tour and I went off to university,’ says Riley. He is unstinting in his praise of the woman who became the mother of the No1 in men’s singles and men’s doubles.

The repartee between Riley and Ogilvie is relaxed but both men have a resolve to grow walking football. Their task has been helped by bookmakers William Hill stepping in with sponsorship.

The benefits of the sport stretch beyond the physical. Ogilvie gave his own experience.

‘When you have finished working, there is a void, not mixing with people, not being with people, and walking football certainly has helped me fill that. Hopefully it helps me keep a bit fitter too,’ he said.

Ogilvie pointed out: ‘The issues you tend to encounter are health. Grief is another one. There are quite a few of the guys who have lost their wives and quite a few who are just sitting on the sofa watching Homes Under the Hammer.’

Walking football, too, has attracted a large cadre of women. ‘One of the things that stood out for me was the number of females playing,’ said Riley. ‘I went along to my first session and there were four female players, three of whom had never kicked a football in their life previously. Walking football got them involved and they really enjoyed it.’

Walking football has made giant leaps in Scotland but the next step is to collate data so cases for funding will be made unanswerable.

‘We need facts or what is called data,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We are trying to do some studies with universities to get that data — physical and mental — and get it to the government. We want to prove the benefits and then we could make this prescriptive through surgeries.

‘We see the benefits day to day anecdotally but that doesn’t bring you the data. Sponsorship helps.

Walking Football attracts thousands of participants at clubs across the country

‘The university studies won’t come overnight because they need to be detailed. But if we could get to the stage where we could prove the benefits, then the NHS and the government would see that proof in black and white.’

This is all serious and proper. But both men were keen to emphasise that the game was fun. Ogilvie said: ‘When I started, I asked someone: “How would you sum up walking football?” He said to me: “It’s a cross between watching Barcelona and the Gurkha warriors”.’

He added: ‘I loved when at the end of an over-75s tournament one player said to another: “Good game, son”.’

The football world has thus moved into a new era. But some things cannot change. Ogilvie said: ‘One of my grandsons, who is 10, came along to watch a session and said two things. Firstly, it is a bit more intense than he thought and second there are no pink boots.’

Riley chimed in: ‘That would be an affront, that would be unacceptable.’

Even in walking football some things are a step too far.

■ Eric Riley and Campbell Ogilvie were speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org
